fields.detail: Directive 12 — the whole problem is now ONE finite SAT/CP-SAT question, not an informal push. QUESTION: can a disjoint triangle pair joined by exactly 2 edges exist AT ALL in a graph that is locally 7K2 with μ=2? Take triangles ABC and DEF, disjoint, with exactly edges A-D and B-E between them. Propagate the constraints outward — every edge lies in a unique triangle (λ=1), every non-adjacent pair has exactly 2 common neighbours (μ=2), every neighbourhood induces a perfect matching (locally 7K2) — and ask whether the configuration extends. Encode the bounded local ball with sat_solver/CP-SAT; UNSAT on a faithful encoding is a real theorem and kills the n3≥1 case, hence (with the re-derived n3=0 branch) the whole problem. ENCODER GATE FIRST: the same encoder must FIND the known configurations in rook(3) and BvLS before any UNSAT is believed — an UNSAT from an untested encoder is a bug report. STATE the radius encoded, and say explicitly what UNSAT at that radius does and does not prove: a local obstruction at radius 2 is NOT a global nonexistence proof, and the note must say so.
